newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Novo Nordisk takes steps to ensure competition - EU.
newsitem.headline: Novo Nordisk takes steps to ensure competition - EU.

text.p: Danish pharmaceutical giant Novo Nordisk has agreed to take steps to meet the European Commission's concerns about competition in the markets for components of the firm's insulin self-injection delivery systems, the Commission said.
The firm made the undertakings after Commission competition policy officials had reached the preliminary conclusion that Novo Nordisk had abused its dominant market position.

The Commission said in a competition policy newsletter that the firm occupied a dominant position on the insulin market and on the markets for components of so-called pen delivery systems, in most EU member states.
The Commission launched the investigation following complaints by U.S.-based medical device maker Becton Dickinson.

"It (the investigation) concluded that it has been abusing its dominance...by in some instances disclaiming liability for the malfunction of its pen products, or refusing to guarantee such products, when they are used in conjunction with the compatible components of other manufacturers," it said.

It was referring to a new method of insulin self-injection, the "insulin pen" system, which Novo Nordisk introduced in 1985 and which the Commission said about a third of all diabetics in Europe now use.
Other firms now produce similar systems, including various components, some of which are compatible with Novo's systems.

The Commission said it had investigated complaints about the explicit disclaimer of liability by Novo Nordisk and "the phrasing of disclaimers in such a way as to create unfounded confusion or uncertainty in the minds of consumers as to the safety or effectiveness of using non-Novo Nordisk components in its pen-delivery systems."
It said Novo, while contesting the allegations, had undertaken to take steps which meet the Commission's concerns.
Novo has now agreed that it will not use liability disclaimers for cases where its products are used with other makers' components, it said.

It has also said that it will not treat other makers' components as incompatible with its systems simply "on the basis of their inability to enable the ancilliary 'function check' for its pen products to be carried out."
The company also agreed to revise the wording of its safety warnings throughout the European Economic Area.
